questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me that my study destination was English-speaking and had a great study life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Melbourne was the perfect city for a study destination. The people were very open-minded, and the city was very vibrant and cool. The university had a lot of great events and was really welcoming. The only bad part about Melbourne was the weather. The weather changed a lot, and sometimes it felt like four different seasons in one day.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. The University of Melbourne has a lot of information on its website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They offered to pick one up from the airport.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was delighted with the orientation and help from the University of Melbourne. It was easy to get in contact with them over the mail. The university has a help centre, which was very helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult, because a lot of the housing was very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You have more freedom if you live off campus. There are more rules if you live on campus e.g. parties.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was quite easy. I didn't run into any problems.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You receive a mail from the university where you have to follow some steps to get approved. It took me around a month to finish it. Remember to apply for your visa early on (some Danish students had some problems receiving it).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can mail the University of Melbourne, and they have a short response time.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very successful. I got the classes I applied for. However, I ended up changing some of the classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to make good research for the classes you want to take and remember you can always change it if you don't like it. It is a good idea to make a broad ”forhåndsgodkendelse”, so you are able to pick another class if you change your mind.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was fine, they were not too difficult. The structure of the assignments was very similar to the way you do it on UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At the University of Melbourne, my courses were more like exercise classes. Whereas at UCPH I have both lectures and exercise classes. Another difference was that the University of Melbourne had an attendance hurdle, I was only allowed to have two absent days from each class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Graphic Design
Internet communication
Marketing communication 
Performance, potential and development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: In Internet communication, I had a really great teacher and you learn a lot of different topics in the course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Travels. You travel a lot when you are on exchange and take a lot of weekend trips.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: More expensive than expected: house rents and food in supermarket

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different sports clubs, language clubs and a wine club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The running club. It is a small team and you don't have to be advanced to be part of it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: For weekend trips, you should go to Wilsons Prom, Mornington Peninsula and Great Ocean Road. For longer trips, you should travel along the East coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It's a Western culture and everyone speaks English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
The easiest way to socialize with the local students is in the class. A lot of the students are very open-minded. 
Get a job. A lot of students have jobs next to their studies. (Bonus: the pay is pretty good in Australia).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is an English-speaking country, and the people are very welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Remember that you only have to pass the subjects, so no reason to stress
- It's okay not to say yes to everything
- Join a sports club. Unimelb has a lot of good sport club options

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The weather in Melbourne changes a lot, so remember to bring both warm and cold clothes with you.
Bring a backpack if you wanna travel afterwards. 
Housing can be expensive so it is a good idea to research housing options beforehand.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the great friends I have met in Melbourne and all the trips we went on.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To find an apartment that was affordable.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
